source: New for #59: the three reference authored events named in the issue (DL's birthday, a storm, first snow of the season), matching plan section 2's own examples of the punctuation cards don't do.
comment: Authored events for the farm district. Where farm.json's cards are drawn under a pacing target, each of these becomes eligible only when its own trigger is met, and while it runs it outranks any card or parameter named in priorityOver. DL's birthday and first snow were random-draw cards in v1 (#41); the plan frames both as authored punctuation, not a draw, so #59 moves them here and gives farm.json two new cards (flockHuddle, farmerMeetsMerchant) to keep the deck at fifteen. Ids are disjoint from farm.json's card ids by construction; the deck test checks it.

timeScale.comment: Same conversion as events/farm.json's timeScale; repeated here so this file stands alone.

events.title: DL's birthday
events.comment: Was the rarest-weighted card in v1 (weight 1 of 100, cooldown 720h); as an authored event it is not a draw at all, it is a date, which is a better fit for something that should happen once and only once a year. The owner decided (2026-09-08, plan section 2 'Time' and section 11 decision 10): Digital Luna's birthday is December 15, a real calendar date, so a world that starts in June waits for it. #83 moves the trigger from a first-day-of-spring `simDate` guess to the real `realDate` this always meant.

trigger.comment: December 15, every real year, regardless of which sim season that calendar date falls in for a given world's seeded calendar (balance/farm.json outsideRules.seasons.calendar).

events.variablesComment: Cosmetic parameters the birthday's own hooks and art read: honey ties loosely to the wildwood's eventual honey economy (plan section 3), a nod not a dependency; ringFormation and heartBubbleCount steer how the flock arranges itself and how many heart bubbles show, values a card has no field for.

start.name: party
start.comment: The flock gathers round DL; heart bubbles all round; DL does her spin. Same flag as the v1 card, now set by the authored event instead of a random draw.

storybook.line: It was {dl}'s birthday. The whole flock came over to say so.

beat.start: A cake bubble over DL and the flock turning to walk towards her, within a second.
beat.end: The ring of sheep drifts apart and DL flops down in the middle, done in.

events.title: A storm off the cliff
events.comment: New authored event for #59: the storm the issue asks for. Triggered by a genuine drought rather than a coin flip, so it reads as relief, not a random inconvenience — a causal design the card schema's conditions could also express, but the trigger's own cooldownSimDays is what stops it firing again the moment the threshold is still crossed a sim-minute later.

trigger.comment: Fires when the mean tuft level crosses below a real drought line, well under wellRunsLow's card-level 0.3. The cooldown gives the grass, and the flock's mood, time to recover before another one is due.

events.variablesComment: Cosmetic parameters for the sim's storm rendering: how far the weather layer shakes the scene and how many thunder beats play. Not stocks; nothing here touches the Ledger beyond the mood hooks below.

start.comment: Driving rain greys the field; higher than fogMorning's 0.35 (clearer, less thick) so the barn stays a clear shape through it.

start.name: storm
start.comment: Sheep crowd into the barn doorway; DL's rain-shepherd priority runs at its hardest.

end.comment: Wet, but the grass will be glad of it.

storybook.line: A storm broke over the cliff and {dl} kept the whole flock under the barn eave.

beat.start: The sky darkens fast, rain hits hard, and every sheep bolts for the barn doorway at once.
beat.end: The rain eases to a drip off the eave and the flock spreads back out, drenched but calm.

events.title: First snow of the season
events.comment: Was the firstSnow card in v1, made rare only by a 720-hour cooldown (the file's own comment called that a proxy for a real 'first' and proposed fixing it here). As an authored event with a predicate trigger and a season-length cooldown it can only mean the actual first snow of THIS winter, which is what the plan's own notion of a 'first' (section 2, the chronicle and the storybook) asks for.

trigger.comment: Fixed for #83's calendar review: a sim day is not a real day. At outsideRules.clock.periodSec = 180 (packages/sim/src/clock.ts:35), one real day = 86400 / 180 = 480 sim days, so the nominal 91-real-day season is 43,680 sim days and a four-season year is about 174,720, not '4 * 91 = 364 sim days' as the old comment here said. cooldownSimDays = 60,000 sits above the longest a winter can realistically run under outsideRules.seasons.calendar (about 109 real days from the anchor gaps plus drift, ≈52,320 sim days — comfortably over even the old naive 101-day/48,480-sim-day estimate) and well under the shortest possible gap to the next winter (about 345 real days, ≈165,600 sim days), so the predicate can lapse and re-arm exactly once each winter, not once every ~15 hours of watched play like the old 30 (and un-rescaled 303) did.

events.variablesComment: Extra snowflake sprites the weather layer spawns for this one flurry, more than an ordinary snowy scene gets.

start.name: firstSnow
start.comment: Sheep look up and stand still; lambs bounce; DL snaps at flakes. Same flag as the v1 card; now authored so it can only mean the first snow, not any snow.

storybook.line: The first snow of the season fell and {dl} tried to catch it in her mouth.

beat.start: Every sheep stops and looks up at the same moment; DL leaps at a flake.
beat.end: The flock goes back to grazing with white on their backs.
